entries.text: The DDL golden corpus passes the runtime's new DDL options (`table_case`, `strip_with_properties`, QuestDB layout fields, SingleStore `DATETIME`, StarRocks `float_as_real`) and records a classification and reason (`equivalent`, `legacy-bug` or `fork-gap`) for every remaining difference; each classification rule verifies the shape of the difference it labels, and a test fails on an unclassified difference or a `fork-gap`. Array columns become `VECTOR(n, F32|F64)` on SingleStore and `VECTOR(n)` on a SQL Server or Azure SQL target with the `vector_type` option; on every other T-SQL target (Synapse, Fabric) the runtime raises a `ValueError` instead of writing an array type those engines reject.
